skill.name: higgsfield-soul-id
skill.description: Train a Higgsfield Soul Character from approved face photos for identity-faithful image and video generation. The skill guides photo selection, submission, waiting, and reuse of the returned Soul ID.
skill.summary: Create a reusable Higgsfield face identity model from user-provided photos.
skill.author: higgsfield-ai

security_audit.summary: The critical issue is the bootstrap command that pipes a remote GitHub installer directly into sh, enabling supply-chain code execution. Most static backtick and reconnaissance alerts are Markdown or visible CLI workflow false positives, but the skill still runs external Higgsfield commands. A semantic finding is included because the workflow auto-uploads biometric face photos through the CLI.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the curl to sh bootstrap. Provide signed release installation steps with checksum verification and require explicit user confirmation before installing anything.

remediation.issue: Face photos are uploaded by the CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit consent checkpoint that names Higgsfield as the destination and confirms each selected path or upload ID before submission.

remediation.issue: Commands use user-provided names and paths.
remediation.suggestion: Document safe argument handling, quote every value, and avoid constructing shell commands from untrusted text.

remediation.issue: Soul reference IDs can be listed or exposed.
remediation.suggestion: Display identifiers only when needed and avoid posting them in shared chat logs or public documentation.

content.value_statement: Creating consistent AI images or videos of the same person is difficult with one-off prompts. This skill guides Higgsfield Soul training from consented photos and returns a reusable identity reference.
actual_capabilities: Collects the required name and 5 to 20 face photos for Soul training.
Checks authentication and paid plan requirements before submission.
Chooses the Soul 2 or cinematic variant based on the target output.
Submits approved local images or upload IDs through the Higgsfield CLI.
Waits for training completion and returns the Soul reference for reuse.
Links to photo quality and troubleshooting guidance for common failures.
limitations: Requires Higgsfield CLI access and an authenticated Higgsfield account.
Requires a paid Higgsfield plan for Soul training.
Depends on clear single-person photos supplied with user consent.
Does not perform one-shot face swaps or create fictional named characters.

output_examples.input: Train a Soul called Maya from these approved portraits.
output_examples.output: Maya is ready. The identity reference is available for reuse in Higgsfield image workflows.

output: Replace group photos, sunglasses, and repeated poses.
Use at least five sharp images with clear face visibility.

output_examples.output: The cinematic Soul variant is selected because the target output is video. Training will continue after confirming the photo set.

best_practices: Use photos with clear consent from the person shown in every image.
Provide varied angles, lighting, expressions, and distances for stronger identity capture.
Confirm account status and plan access before starting long training jobs.
anti_patterns: Do not upload group photos, filtered images, or photos with covered faces.
Do not train a Soul from photos of a person who has not approved the use.
Do not expose Soul IDs in shared chat logs or public documentation.

faq.question: What is a Higgsfield Soul Character?
faq.answer: It is a reusable identity model trained from a person's face photos for Higgsfield generation workflows.

faq.question: How many photos should I provide?
faq.answer: Use 5 to 20 photos. Eight to twelve varied, sharp images usually work best.

faq.question: Does this require a paid plan?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill notes that Soul training requires a Basic or higher Higgsfield plan.

faq.question: Can I use uploaded asset IDs instead of local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow accepts local photo paths or existing image upload IDs.

faq.question: Can this create a one-shot face swap?
faq.answer: No. Use Higgsfield generation with an input image for one-shot face replacement workflows.

faq.question: How should I handle privacy?
faq.answer: Use only consented photos and avoid sharing Soul IDs outside the approved workflow.
